final_message:
I found and fixed 8 bugs, and all 24 tests now pass (8 were failing before). I didn't touch the tests. I also checked the cases the tests don't cover with my own spot checks.

The bugs:

1. **`amounts.py:parse_amount`**: amounts in parentheses like `(45.10)` had the brackets removed but were never made negative.
2. **`amounts.py:parse_amount`**: the only validation was whether `Decimal()` accepted the string, so it let through things the README doesn't allow: `1e3`, `1_000`, `1,,2`, `12,34` and `(-5)`. It now checks the format strictly: digits with optional comma groups of three, plus an optional decimal part.
3. **`amounts.py:round_money`**: floats went straight into `Decimal()`, so `2.675` came out as `2.67`. Floats are now converted through their printed form first, so they round half up as the README says.
4. **`currency.py:convert`**: the rates were applied backwards (`amount * src / dst` instead of `amount / src * dst`). Same-currency conversions hid this, but EUR→USD was wrong.
5. **`currency.py:minor_units`**: it looked up the lower-case code in a table keyed `"JPY"`, so yen always got 2 decimals instead of 0. It now uses the same code handling as `convert`, so an unknown code raises `ValueError` here too.
6. **`vat.py:vat_rate_for`**: category names weren't lower-cased or trimmed, so `"Food"` or `" books "` got the standard 20% rate.
7. **`invoice.py:line_total`**: VAT was worked out on the price before discount instead of after.
8. **`dates.py:days_in_range`**: the end date was left out, so a single-day range came back empty.

Two judgement calls in the new number check: `5.` and `.5` are still accepted, and so is `$-12.50` (the old code allowed it on purpose). The README doesn't mention any of these, so tighten them if you'd rather.

`REPORT.md` has one line per bug in the format you gave.
